packs.title: Bays & Beyond
packs.promise: Meet Dubrovnik beyond the walls, from a restored park to everyday harbour life.

q.s: Curate a small conversation between two artworks.
st: Choose two works on display that suggest different moods to you. Use visible colour, marks, pose or spacing rather than guessing an artist’s intention.
Read their labels and record each title if available, or a precise description if not.
Imagine the works shown together. Write a short reason why their disagreement would make a good pair.
Choose which you would encounter first and explain how the order changes your experience.

q.s: Give one real detail a fictional journey.
st: Choose one visible harbour detail, such as a moored small boat, a rope seen from a distance or a reflection.
Invent three short frames: before a departure, a moment of waiting and a return. Keep the real detail in every frame.
Change only one thing between each frame: the light, a fictional object’s position or the mood.
Sketch the frames or write a sentence for each. Make clear that the journey is invented; no real passenger needs a backstory.

q.s: Sort the shoreline without collecting anything.
st: From one safe position, look for three different visible ways land meets water, such as a beach edge, rock or a constructed wall. A distant example counts.
Sort them as mostly natural, mostly built or uncertain, giving a visible reason rather than a geological claim.
Choose one boundary that would change in appearance as waves move. Describe the change you actually see, or predict it clearly as a guess.

packs.title: Stone & Small Stories
packs.promise: Find small stories in the Old Town’s stone, squares and harbour.

q.s: See what a small carving leaves behind.
st: Choose two visible carved capitals from the permitted lower-cloister visitor route. Notice how their details differ without touching them.
Pick one, look away briefly and draw or describe its most memorable detail. Looking down at blank paper works too.
Look back and add one thing you missed. Compare your first impression with the corrected version.

q.s: Give a square four lines and one small twist.
st: Choose one ordinary detail in the square and a short word it suggests: perhaps “still”, “light” or a word of your own.
Write four short lines about the place. Use your chosen word twice with a different meaning or feeling the second time.
Read the lines silently and remove one word that does not earn its place. Keep the final version private if you prefer.

q.s: Let a facade do more than look impressive.
st: Find three visible details: one that appears to decorate, one that supports or encloses, and one that casts a shadow. A single detail may have more than one role.
Describe each from where you stand without touching stone or blocking an entrance.
Move one detail into another category and explain why it can do two jobs. A drawn arrow or a sentence is enough.
